IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.claim: These readers retain the hāʾ in liaison in لم يتسنه and the listed parallel forms; all readers retain it at pause, and all keep it in the two further al-Ḥāqqa forms in both positions.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر هذه الحروف كلها بإثبات الهاء في الوصل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r3.claim: Ḥamza drops the hāʾ in liaison in all the listed forms; like everyone, he retains it at pause.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī drops the hāʾ in liaison only in لم يتسنه and اقتده, retaining it in the remaining listed forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p188/r4.anchor: وكان الكسائي يحذف الهاء في الوصل من قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.claim: Most readers retain hāʾ al-sakt in the connected and paused forms for book, reckoning, wealth, and power, and also in mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: كتابيه، وحسابيه في موضعيهما وماليه وسلطانيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin deletes the hāʾ and silences the yāʾ; Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash delete it only in connected speech, while Ḥamza does so for selected forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: بحذفها وصلا ووقفا وإسكان الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.claim: Al-Zuhrawī calls retaining hāʾ in connected speech an error, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because the transmitted reading is mass-transmitted and must be accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.anchor: ليس كما قال، بل ذلك منقول نقل التواتر فوجب قبوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r14.claim: ما أغنى عني ماليه may be a plain denial that his wealth helped, spoken in regret, or a self-reproaching question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r14.anchor: يجوز أن يكون نفيا محضا، أخبر بذلك متأسفا على ماله حيث لم ينفعه ويجوز أن يكون استفهاما

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r1.claim: Mā aghnā is either a denial or a reproachful question: what benefit did his wealth bring him?
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r1.anchor: { ما أغنى } نفي أو استفهام على وجه الإنكار أي أي شيء أغنى عني ما كان لي من اليسار

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r2.claim: Rāzī compares the lonely arrival here with 19:80, “and he comes to Us alone.”

RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.claim: The blessed were first described in joy and good living, eating and drinking; correspondingly the wretched are introduced through grief before their restraints and food.
RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r7.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى ذكر سرور السعداء أولا ، ثم ذكر أحوالهم في العيش الطيب وفي الأكل والشرب ، كذا ههنا

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r21.claim: The negative mā may instead be interrogative, making the line a rhetorical question: “What has my wealth availed me?”
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r21.anchor: The negative particle mā in this verse could also be understood as an interrogative particle, in which case the verse is understood as a rhetorical question

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r22.claim: The line echoes the Quranic theme that worldly advantages usually do not help in the next life; 18:46 contrasts worldly wealth and children with enduring righteous deeds.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r22.anchor: the broader Quranic theme that the things that provide advantages in this world are usually of no avail in the next

TAB-FULL:v23p236/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r1.claim: The speaker’s worldly wealth did not protect him from any of God’s punishment.
TAB-FULL:v23p236/r1.anchor: يعني أنه لم يدفع عنه ماله الذي كان يملكه في الدنيا من عذاب الله شيئا

TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.claim: These are words of regret: he had treated wealth and power as keys to happiness, protection from harm, and control of what he desired, and had labored for them while turning from God and truth.
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r2.anchor: كلمتا تحسر يقولهما حيث يرى خيبة سعيه في الدنيا فإنه كان يحسب أن مفتاح سعادته في الحياة

TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.claim: Seeing that worldly means have collapsed and wealth and children cannot help on this Day, he laments his wealth’s uselessness and his power’s failure; regret now avails nothing.
TABATABAI:69:27-36/r3.anchor: فلما شاهد تقطع الأسباب وأنه في يوم لا ينفع فيه مال ولا بنون ذكر عدم نفع ما له وبطلان سلطانه

BURSEVI:v10p110/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r1.claim: On the negative reading, the phrase means that the wealth did not ward off any of the afterlife's punishment; the object is omitted.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r1.anchor: أيلم يدفع عني شيئا من عذاب الآخرة على أن ما نافية والمفعول محذوف

BURSEVI:v10p110/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r2.claim: On the relative reading, ماليه includes worldly wealth and followers; the prepositional lām attached to the possessive yā broadens the reference.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r2.anchor: المال والاتباع على أن ما موصولة واللام جارة داخلة على ياء المتكلم ليعم مثل الاتباع

BURSEVI:v10p110/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r3.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p110/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes the wording as both negation and a rhetorical question of denial: what did his worldly means avail him?
BURSEVI:v10p110/r3.anchor: الكشاف" ما أغنى نفي واستفهام على وجه الإنكار أي أي شيء أغنى عني

BURSEVI:v10p110/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r4.claim: The apparent meaning is his worldly money alone: it distracted and harmed him instead of helping, as in the cited verses about wealth failing its owner.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن مالية هو المال المضاف إلى ياء المتكلم أي لم يغن عني المال الذي جمعته في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p110/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r5.claim: The author rejects the majority exegetical generalization to wealth and followers as departing from the Quran's apparent wording.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r5.anchor: فما ذهب إليه أكثر أهل التفسير من التعميم عدول عما ورد به ظاهر القرآن

BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.claim: The wealth wording alludes to wealthy Quraysh leaders such as al-Walid, while the mention of lost power exposes their worldly status.
BURSEVI:v10p110/r10.anchor: يدل على الأول على أن فيه تعريضا بنحو الوليد من رؤساء قريش وأهل ثروتهم

THALABI:v10p30/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p30/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p30/r12.claim: Most commentators take the lines to mean that his wealth did not help and his proof or argument has vanished.
THALABI:v10p30/r12.anchor: ذهبت عني حجتي عن أكثر المفسرين،

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r22.claim: Mā can be a negation or rhetorical question: what use was my wealth? It helped him not at all; if it helped anyone, it was others, while he kept regret and punishment.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r22.anchor: neye yaradı benden yana malım? Hiçbir şeye yaramadı

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.claim: Soon after boasting of conquering fate, Fannā Khusraw went mad and died repeating that his wealth and authority had failed him.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r2.anchor: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ diye diye can verip gitmişti.

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.claim: The final hā in kitābiyeh, hisābiyeh, māliyeh, and sultāniyeh is hāʾ al-sakt, used at pause after fatḥa and always read with sukūn; the underlying forms end in -iya.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.anchor: “Kitâbiyeh, hisâbiyeh, mâliyeh, sultâniyeh” fâsılalarında ها fetha üzerine vakf için hâ-i sekittir. Dâima sâkin okunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r3.claim: That wish is useless, and the wealth he accumulated without regard for lawful and unlawful cannot avert punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r3.anchor: Böyle bir temenni orada bir işe yaramayacağı gibi, dünyada helâl haram demeden biriktirmiş olduğu malı da kendisine verilecek cezayı önlemeyecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.claim: Wealth, property, sovereignty, status, and power all disappear; only a person's good or bad beliefs and deeds remain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r4.anchor: mal, mülk, saltanat, makam, güç vb. dünyaya ait ne varsa hepsi yok olup gitmiş, sadece insanın olumlu veya olumsuz inanç ve amelleri kalmıştır

BURHAN:v4p430/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.claim: Hāʾ al-sakt marks a pause and follows a built ending to preserve its vowel; it is normally deleted in connected speech, while the codex spellings support stopping on it.
BURHAN:v4p430/r6.anchor: وتلحق وقفا لبيان الحركة وإنما تلحق بحركة بناء لا تشبه حركة الإعراب

BURHAN:v4p430/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.speaker: حمزة
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.claim: The readers retain hāʾ in connection in كتابيه and حسابيه on pausal intent; Hamza deletes it in three other words when connecting but retains it at a stop.

ITQAN:v2p520/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p520/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p520/r3.claim: Nūn al-wiqāya precedes the first-person yāʾ after verbs and particles, and occurs with ladun and with min or ʿan, as in the cited verses.
ITQAN:v2p520/r3.anchor: ونون الوقاية وتلحق ياء المتكلم المنصوبة بفعل نحو ﴿ فاعبدني ﴾ ﴿ ليحزنني ﴾ أو حرف نحو ﴿ يا ليتني كنت معهم ﴾ ﴿ إنني أنا الله ﴾

ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.claim: A pause hāʾ is appended to forms such as māliyah and sulṭāniyah; readers also pronounce it at the pauses on plural verse endings.
ITQAN:v2p521#3/r2.anchor: وحرف للغيبة وهو اللاحق لإيا وللسكت نحو ﴿ ما هيه ﴾ ﴿ كتابيه ﴾ ﴿ حسابيه ﴾ ﴿ سلطانيه ﴾ ﴿ ماليه ﴾

ITQAN:v3p269/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.claim: The pause hāʾ is used at verse endings in māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and mā hiyah.
ITQAN:v3p269/r11.anchor: إثبات هاء السكت نحو ﴿ ماليه ﴾ ﴿ سلطانيه ﴾ ﴿ ما هيه ﴾

TUSTARI:69:28/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:28/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:69:28/r1.claim: His abundant wealth did not help because he paid none of God's due from it and did not maintain kinship.
TUSTARI:69:28/r1.anchor: كثرة مالي، حيث لم أؤد منه حق الله، ولم أصل به القرابة

NAHHAS:v5p21/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p21/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p21/r18.claim: ما is accusative as an object of أغنى, or it can be a non-parsing negator.
NAHHAS:v5p21/r18.anchor: ما في موضع نصب بأغنى ويجوز أن تكون نافية لا موضع لها

SAMIN-DURR:69:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:28/r1.claim: ما أغنى may be negation or a reproachful question the speaker asks himself.
SAMIN-DURR:69:28/r1.anchor: قوله: { ما أغنى }: يجوز أن يكون نفيا، وأن يكون استفهام توبيخ لنفسه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.claim: The hāʾ endings in the Resurrection scene convey exhaustion, hardship, and pain; the author relates the sound to sighing and the long, severe wait for intercession.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p90/r2.anchor: إذن استخدام حرف الهاء في فواصل هذه السورة يدل على التعب والعناء والألم والهاء مأخوذة من الآه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r1.claim: With a first-person possessive yāʾ, the final yāʾ may be either vowelled or quiescent, as in كتابي and كتابيه.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r1.anchor: من سكّن الياء يقول (كتابي) ومن فتح الياء يقول (كتابيه)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.claim: The hāʾ endings in the judgment-day words evoke the exhausted people’s sigh, hardship, and pain during the long ordeal; the sound choice reflects the scene’s psychological weight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p540/r2.anchor: إذن استخدام حرف الهاء في فواصل هذه السورة يدل على التعب والعناء والألم والهاء مأخوذة من الآه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.claim: Kufr is broader than denial: Al Imran 3:10 names wealth and children, while other verses show followers, authority, gods, and intercessors cannot help; a particular instance of disbelief is therefore called denial.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1000/r1.anchor: نلاحظ قلنا أن الكفر أعمّ من التكذيب، ننظر في الآيات: ذكر في آل عمران حالة جزئية

NASHR:v1p223/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p223/r3.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p223/r3.claim: Reciters differ over assimilating or clearly pronouncing the two hāʾs in maliyah halaka; the majority make them clear because the first is hāʾ al-sakt.
NASHR:v1p223/r3.anchor: وقد اختلف في إدغام: ماليه هلك وإظهاره مع اجتماع المثلين والجمهور على الإظهار

NASHR:v2p21/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r1.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v2p21/r1.claim: Makki argues that anyone using naql in “كتابيَهْ إني” should assimilate the hāʾ in “ماليه هلك,” since naql treats it as original; he nevertheless says he read with izhar and considers it the correct practice.
NASHR:v2p21/r1.anchor: وقال مكي في تبصرته: يلزم من ألقى الحركة في كتابيه إني أن يدغم ماليه هلك

NASHR:v2p21/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v2p21/r2.claim: Abu Shama says izhar here requires a slight pause; if the reader truly connects, the sound must either assimilate or be vocalized, and omitting both amounts to an unrecognized pause.
NASHR:v2p21/r2.anchor: قال أبو شامة يعني بالإظهار أن يقف على ماليه هلك وقفة لطيفة

NASHR:v2p21/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن السخاوي
NASHR:v2p21/r3.claim: Al-Sakhawi prefers stopping because the hāʾ was added for pause; if connected, he prefers izhar since the hāʾ remains intended as paused and the following hāʾ is separate.
NASHR:v2p21/r3.anchor: والمختار فيه أن يوقف عليه؛ لأن الهاء إنما اجتلبت للوقف فلا يجوز أن توصل

NASHR:v2p21/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p21/r4.claim: The author finds Abu Shama’s explanation most precise and follows al-Dani: with tahqiq, make a light pause on hāʾ while notionally connecting; with ilqa, connect and assimilate because hāʾ is treated as original.
NASHR:v2p21/r4.anchor: وما قاله أبو شامة أقرب إلى التحقيق، وأحرى بالدراية والتدقيق

NASHR:v1p18/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18/r1.claim: The author permits rare analogy when it conflicts with no explicit transmission, consensus, or principle, citing inferred idghām in māliyah halak and qāla rajul/rajulān by analogy with qāla rabb.
NASHR:v1p18/r1.anchor: ونقل (كتابيه اني) وإدغام (ماليه هلك) قياسا عليه

NASHR:v1p18/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r6.speaker: السخاوي
NASHR:v1p18/r6.claim: Al-Sakhāwī says mixing variant readings is an error.
NASHR:v1p18/r6.anchor: الإمام أبو الحسن علي بن محمد السخاوي في كتابه جمال القراء:

NASHR:v1p18/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r7.speaker: النووي
NASHR:v1p18/r7.claim: Al-Nawawī says to stay with one of the seven readings while the discourse remains connected; after it ends one may switch, though maintaining one reading throughout the session is preferable.
NASHR:v1p18/r7.anchor: الحبر العلامة أبو زكريا النووي في كتابه التبيان:

NASHR:v1p18/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق الجعبري
NASHR:v1p18/r8.claim: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ gives the same sense; al-Jaʿbarī says combining readings is forbidden within a word or across connected words, and otherwise disliked.
NASHR:v1p18/r8.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الجعبري: والتركيب ممتنع في كلمة وفي كلمتين

NASHR:v2p142/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p142/r7.speaker: حمزة، ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p142/r7.claim: Hamza and Yaʿqūb omit the hāʾ of māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and māhiyah in connection; the others retain it in both positions.
NASHR:v2p142/r7.anchor: فحذف الهاء من الثلاثة في الوصل حمزة ويعقوب

QIRAAT-ER:69:28:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:2#1/r1.claim: The standard Form IV perfect aghnā means availed or sufficed.

QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#1/r1.claim: The standard reading pauses with saktah on the hāʾ of māliyah before halaka in 69:29; the hāʾ marks the possessive suffix at pause.
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading with saktah: pause on hāʾ of māliyah before halaka (69:29)

QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#2/r1.claim: Without the pausal hāʾ, māliya runs directly into halaka; -ya remains the first-person possessive suffix.
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#2/r1.anchor: Without pausal hāʾ: māliya runs directly into halaka; -ya is the 1sg possessive suffix

QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#3/r1.claim: Assimilation merges the hāʾ at the end of māliyah into the initial hāʾ of halaka in continuous recitation.
QIRAAT-ER:69:28:4#3/r1.anchor: Assimilation: hāʾ of māliyah assimilates into hāʾ of halaka — continuous articulation merging the two words

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r1.claim: On the primary parsing, the first mā is negative and the mā in māliya is relative, serving as subject of “availed”; its object is omitted and “was mine” is its relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r1.anchor: على أن ما في ما أغنى نافية وما في ماليه موصولة فاعل أغنى ومفعوله محذوف وليه جار ومجرور في موضع الصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r2.claim: The primary sense is that none of his worldly wealth or comparable assets, such as followers, availed him; this reading more readily includes followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r2.anchor: أي ما أغنى عني شيئا الذي كان لي في الدنيا من المال ونحوه كالأتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, mā is interrogative and māliya means “my wealth,” yielding a rhetorical question; followers fit only by implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما في ما أغنى استفهامية للإنكار وماليه على احتمالية أي أي شيء أغنى عني مالي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r8.claim: His wealth did not protect him from any of God's punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r8.anchor: {ما أغنى عني ماليه} لم يدفع عني من عذاب الله شيئا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r6.claim: “My wealth” includes property and followers; mā may be a negation with an omitted object, or an interrogative object of “benefit,” making a denial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r6.anchor: مالي من المال والتبع وما نفى

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.speaker: حمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.claim: Ḥamza drops both final hāʾs in connected reading; the other readers retain them in both connected and paused forms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «عني» «مالي» «عني سلطاني» بحذف الهاءين في الوصل والباقون بإثباتها في الحالين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r9.claim: On the declarative reading, the object of “benefit” is omitted so the denial encompasses every possible benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r9.anchor: والمفعول على هذا التقدير محذوف للتعميم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r10.claim: Alternatively, he asks a rhetorical question that reproaches himself for believing wealth could rescue him from the reckoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r10.anchor: أو مستفهما استفهام إنكار على نفسه وتوبيخ حيث سولت له ما أثمر له كل سوء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r11.claim: His wealth had been withheld from what was due to God and used to exalt himself above God's servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r11.anchor: أي الذي منعت منه حق الله وتعظمت به على عباده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r4.claim: The speaker is a wealthy, powerful disbelieving leader; his wealth failed him, and followers grieve when they see their model’s ruin, implicitly targeting Abū Jahl and Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r4.anchor: قال : { ما أغنى عني ماليه } ، أي يقول ذلك من كان ذا مال وذا سلطان من ذلك الفريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r5.claim: Aghnā ʿannī contains near graphic paronomasia, like the cited phrase about pride deceiving its possessor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r5.anchor: وفي { أغنى عني } الجناس الخطي ولو مع اختلاف قليل كما في قولهم ( غرك عزك فصار قصارى ذلك ذلك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.speaker: حمزة وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.claim: Ḥamza and Khalaf omit the hāʾ of māliya and sulṭāniya in connected recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p136/r8.anchor: إلا أن حمزة وخلفا قرآ هنا { ما أغنى عني ماليه هلك عني سلطانيه } بدون هاء في حالة الوصل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.claim: Neither wealth nor worldly standing protected him from God's punishment; he is left alone without helper or rescuer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r4.anchor: أي: لم يدفع عني مالي ولا جاهي عذاب الله وبأسه، بل خلص الأمر إلي وحدي، فلا معين لي ولا مجير.

JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.claim: Hamza and Yaqub drop the final h in connection for māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿa; all retain it at pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب: ماليه وسلطانيه وفي سورة (القارعة) (ما هيه) بحذف الهاء في الوصل،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r3.claim: ما أغنى may be a negation or rhetorical question: ‘what benefit did my wealth give me?’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p607#2/r3.anchor: ما أغنى } نفي أو استفهام على وجه الإنكار ، أي : أي شيء أغنى عني

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r7.claim: His abundant worldly wealth did not protect him in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r7.anchor: أن كثرة ماله في الدنيا لم يمنع عنه في الآخرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r8.claim: His desire for worldly adornment and wealth distracted him from the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r8.anchor: لأن رغبته في زينة الدنيا وكثرة المال هو الذي ألهاه عن الآخرة

MUQATIL:69:25-32/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r4.claim: His wealth did not protect him from the Fire.
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r4.anchor: { مآ أغنى عني ماليه } [آية: 28] من النار { هلك عني سلطانيه } [آية: 29] يقول: ضلت عني يومئد حجتي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#4/r1.claim: The wealth he accumulated in worldly life did not benefit him; the object “anything” is omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#4/r1.anchor: أى لم ينفعنى ما جمعته فى الدنيا فما نفعى والمفعول محذوف اى شيئا
